answer: Guarantor liability is the hinge: every fresh agent enters the economy only when an established peer stakes a slice of its own rewards behind it. If the newcomer turns out to be a sybil clone, the guarantor has its bonded stake slashed in full, so veterans vet whom they vouch for. Trust climbs the ridge slowly, fraud drains the oasis of easy gains, and a clone farm returns sink to their nadir long before minting extra identities pays off.
